newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST - OECD sees Polish 1997 CPI down to 14 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - OECD sees Polish 1997 CPI down to 14 pct.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) on Monday predicted Poland's inflation should fall to around 18 percent year-on-year at the end of 1996 and 14 percent at the end of 1997.
In October, year-on-year consumer price growth was 19.5 percent, down from 21.6 percent at the end of 1995.

The OECD said in its second annual economic survey devoted to Poland that the official 13 percent inflation target for the end of 1997 was achievable if financial discipline was tight and the awaited overhaul of the ailing pensions system began.
"Targets are feasible provided that the stance of financial policies is prudent enough, and that serious reform of the pension system starts... which would bolster national savings," it said.
The OECD also said that a further de-indexation of nominal incomes would limit cost-push pressures next year.
